focus: Close the evidence-integrity gap where realtime reflection cubemaps could be completed under one renderable geometry/material/texture state and reused for native-4K stills after that state changed while the physical SummerSun/sky hash remained identical.

problemFound.summary: The existing asynchronous reflection waiter hashed SummerSun, sky, ambient SH, reflection/fog and global shadow/LOD settings at request, every Editor poll, completion and pre-still, but did not bind active renderer transforms, mesh state, material state or texture bindings. A stable lighting hash therefore did not by itself prove that the cubemap and still described the same renderable scene/material state.

boundState: renderer world transforms, bounds, shadow/probe/sorting/motion-vector state
shared mesh identity, asset dependency hash, vertex/submesh/index/bounds invariants and bounded vertex samples for runtime meshes
ordered shared materials with current Editor serialization, shader/keyword/render-queue/GI/instancing state and asset dependency hash
common PBR/detail texture bindings, dimensions, mip/filter/wrap/aniso state, UV scale/offset and texture dependency hashes
implementation.hiddenOverridePolicy: Active Renderer MaterialPropertyBlock overrides are rejected from formal reflection/still evidence until arbitrary override payloads are explicitly fingerprinted. This prevents shared-material hashing from leaving an untracked per-renderer shader override channel.
implementation.existingWaiterReuse: The inner render-state SHA-256 is folded into QualityBlockReflectionLightingStateFingerprint. Therefore the existing QualityBlockReflectionProbeAwaiter request/every-observed-Editor-poll/completion/pre-still equality checks now fail closed on either physical-lighting drift or renderable scene/material drift without weakening the existing async RenderID proof.

unityApiDocumentationChecked: Unity Texture mipmapCount and sampling properties

limitations: No Unity 6000.3.0f1 runner/editor artifact exists yet, so API compatibility and runtime cost are not claimed as verified.

Runtime procedural mesh protection uses identity/count/bounds plus a bounded deterministic 64-vertex sample rather than hashing every vertex on every Editor poll; actual pixels remain authoritative for subtle unsampled in-place deformation.
Arbitrary shader globals/native-plugin state outside the recorded scene/material/texture scope is not claimed to be cryptographically covered.
MaterialPropertyBlock is therefore rejected rather than partially fingerprinted.
Hash equality proves evidence-state coherence only; it does not prove physically correct Fresnel, texture quality, geometry quality or cinematography.

implementationReadiness.reason: The only reserved readiness points remain the 7-point actual Unity compile/runtime verification blocker. This run strengthens evidence coherence but does not satisfy that blocker.

expectedVisualScoreImpact: Material/PBR 20: prevents a reflection cubemap from being accepted after shared material/shader/texture state changed before still capture; actual points remain pixel-reviewed only.
Lighting/shadows/reflections 15: extends the existing SummerSun/sky/ambient coherence proof so reflected scene content and material response are also state-identical across the async probe boundary.
Texture/microdetail 10: binds texture assignment, dependency hash and sampling state across probe/still evidence.
Geometry/construction 20: binds active renderer transforms, bounds and mesh invariants, reducing stale-cubemap risk after geometry movement/replacement.
Weathering 10 and Cinematic 5: prevents stable lighting from masking a changed residue/material state before final evidence.
Automatic Visual Fidelity impact: 0 points because no actual Unity pixels exist.
nextBlocker: Unity 6000.3.0f1 compile/runtime. At first Runner availability stop speculative expansion and run Prepare Complete Native 4K Review Packet. First verify that reflection-lighting-state-v2 remains identical across request, every observed poll, completion and pre-still without exceeding the 30 second probe wait. If the new property-block guard fails, inspect whether any intentional benchmark renderer uses MaterialPropertyBlock and explicitly fingerprint its exact override payload before permitting it; do not disable the guard. Then inspect sealed 3840x2160 hero/oblique/grazing pixels and 100% crops before assigning any Visual Fidelity points.
